This script draws the three figures: the cohort flowchart (Figure 1), the survival curve (Figure 2) and the odds ratios from the final model (Figure 3), in the house style shared with the COHERO analysis. The figures are written to `figures/`, which is not in the repository; they appear on this site only after USRDS review clears them.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/figures.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/blob/main/R/figures.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following helper files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/blob/main/R/setup.R)
-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/blob/main/R/functions.R)
-   [`R/plot_style.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/blob/main/R/plot_style.R)
-   [`R/create_cohort.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/blob/main/R/create_cohort.R)
-   [`R/fit_models.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/blob/main/R/fit_models.R)
-   [`R/tables.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/blob/main/R/tables.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from the script when this page is rendered.
:::

## Figure 1: the cohort

The flowchart is drawn from the same object that built the cohort, so the two cannot disagree. If any box holds 1 to 10 people, the figure is not saved and the run warns.

**Functions used:** [`flowchart_small_counts()`](functions.qmd#small-count-rules-for-figures).

```{r}
#| label: figure-1
#| eval: false
```

**How this differs from the published figure.** The [published flowchart](results.qmd#figure-1.-flowchart-of-selection-of-relevant-ktrs-from-the-usrds-database) shows the starting totals and the final cohort only. This one shows every exclusion in the plan's order, with its count, because a reader cannot judge who was left out otherwise (STROBE and RECORD item 13). Its boxes therefore will not line up one for one with the published ones.

## Figure 2: survival

The survival curve has its 95% confidence band and, below it, the number still at risk and the running totals of deaths and censored people. A time appears in that table only if no count shown there, or the change since the previous time, is from 1 to 10, and the curve stops at the last such time (`km_reportable_times()` on the [Functions](functions.qmd#small-count-rules-for-figures) page). A dashed line marks 6 months.

**Functions used:** [`km_reportable_times()`](functions.qmd#small-count-rules-for-figures), [`theme_publication()`](plot_style.qmd#the-publication-theme) and [`save_figure()`](plot_style.qmd#saving-a-figure).

```{r}
#| label: figure-2
#| eval: false
```

**How this differs from the published figure.** The [published curve](results.qmd#figure-2.-kaplan-meier-survival-curve-for-the-1265-kidney-transplant-recipients-hospitalized-with-cryptococcosis) shows years on the axis, the number at risk every 5 years, and no confidence band. This one follows the KMunicate recommendations: the 95% confidence band, and below the curve the numbers at risk, censored and dead at each time shown, so a reader can see how much information lies behind each part of the curve. Time is in months, because the outcome is at 6 months.

## Figure 3: odds ratios

Each variable kept in the final model, with its adjusted odds ratio and 95% confidence interval on a log scale, and the numbers printed beside it.

**Functions used:** [`tidy_odds_ratios()`](functions.qmd#odds-ratios) and [`save_figure()`](plot_style.qmd#saving-a-figure).

```{r}
#| label: figure-3
#| eval: false
```

**How this differs from the published figure.** The [published forest plot](results.qmd#figure-3.-multivariable-logistic-regression-analysis-of-predictors-of-6-month-mortality) uses a linear axis from 0 to 10. This one uses a log scale, on which halving and doubling the odds are the same distance from 1, so effects in either direction can be compared by eye; the estimate and interval are printed beside each row so no value has to be read off the axis.
